lines.s: You hear two friends discussing an exhibition they have just visited.
lines.zh: 你聽到兩個朋友在討論剛看完的展覽。
lines.en: You hear two friends discussing an exhibition they have just visited.

lines.s: Well, the reviews were right about the lighting — it was stunning. But I can't say the paintings themselves did much for me.
lines.zh: 嗯，評論說燈光很棒，確實很驚豔。可是畫作本身，老實說沒讓我有什麼感覺。
lines.en: Well, the reviews were right about the lighting — it was stunning. But I can't say the paintings themselves did much for me.

lines.s: Really? I thought the later works were extraordinary. Though I agree they tried to cram far too much into such a small space.
lines.zh: 真的嗎？我覺得後期的作品很了不起。不過我同意，他們在那麼小的空間塞了太多東西。
lines.en: Really? I thought the later works were extraordinary. Though I agree they tried to cram far too much into such a small space.

lines.s: Exactly. You couldn't step back to look at anything properly.
lines.zh: 就是說啊，根本沒辦法退後好好看任何一件。
lines.en: Exactly. You couldn't step back to look at anything properly.

ask.s: What did the woman think of the exhibition?
ask.zh: 女的覺得展覽怎麼樣？
ask.en: What did the woman think of the exhibition?

options.t: She was impressed by how it was presented.

explain.zh: 「燈光……確實很驚豔」，但畫作沒讓她有感覺。
explain.en: The lighting impressed her; the paintings did not.

ask.s: What do they agree about?
ask.zh: 他們對什麼看法一致？
ask.en: What do they agree about?

options.t: the quality of the later works

explain.zh: 男的說「在那麼小的空間塞了太多東西」，女的說「就是說啊」。
explain.en: Too much crammed into a small space.

lines.s: You hear a man talking about working from home.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位男士談在家工作。
lines.en: You hear a man talking about working from home.

lines.s: When my company let us work from home, I thought it would be a dream. And in some ways it is — no commute, no noisy office. But I hadn't realised how much I relied on bumping into people. Half my best ideas came from chats in the corridor. Now I make a point of going in twice a week, just for that.
lines.zh: 公司讓我們在家工作時，我以為是美夢成真。某些方面確實是——不用通勤，沒有吵雜的辦公室。但我沒發現自己有多依賴和人不期而遇。我一半的好點子都來自走廊上的閒聊。現在我特意每週進公司兩次，就是為了這個。
lines.en: When my company let us work from home, I thought it would be a dream. And in some ways it is — no commute, no noisy office. But I hadn't realised how much I relied on bumping into people. Half my best ideas came from chats in the corridor. Now I make a point of going in twice a week, just for that.

ask.s: What did the man fail to anticipate about working from home?
ask.zh: 男的對在家工作沒料到的是什麼？
ask.en: What did the man fail to anticipate about working from home?

options.t: how much he would miss commuting
how noisy his home would be

explain.zh: 「我沒發現自己有多依賴和人不期而遇」，好點子來自走廊閒聊。

ask.s: Why does he now go into the office?
ask.zh: 他現在為什麼進公司？
ask.en: Why does he now go into the office?

options.t: to have informal contact with colleagues

explain.zh: 「特意每週進公司兩次，就是為了這個」：和同事聊天。

lines.s: You hear part of a radio discussion about language learning apps.
lines.zh: 你聽到一段關於語言學習 App 的廣播討論。
lines.en: You hear part of a radio discussion about language learning apps.

lines.s: The apps are excellent at what they do — building vocabulary, making practice a habit. The trouble is that people assume a daily streak means they're becoming fluent.
lines.zh: 這些 App 在它們擅長的事上做得很好——累積單字、讓練習變成習慣。問題是大家以為每天連續打卡就代表自己越來越流利。
lines.en: The apps are excellent at what they do — building vocabulary, making practice a habit. The trouble is that people assume a daily streak means they're becoming fluent.

lines.s: And they're not?
lines.zh: 那其實不是嗎？
lines.en: And they're not?

lines.s: Not without real conversation. You can know three thousand words and still freeze when someone asks you a simple question. The apps are a starting point, not a substitute.
lines.zh: 沒有真正的對話就不是。你可以認識三千個單字，別人問個簡單問題時還是會愣住。App 是起點，不是替代品。
lines.en: Not without real conversation. You can know three thousand words and still freeze when someone asks you a simple question. The apps are a starting point, not a substitute.

ask.s: What does the woman say the apps do well?
ask.zh: 女的說 App 擅長什麼？
ask.en: What does the woman say the apps do well?

explain.zh: 「累積單字、讓練習變成習慣」。
explain.en: Building vocabulary and a habit of practice.

ask.s: What is her main concern?
ask.zh: 她最主要的擔心是什麼？
ask.en: What is her main concern?

options.t: The vocabulary taught is too basic.

explain.zh: 「大家以為每天連續打卡就代表自己越來越流利」。
explain.en: People assume a streak means fluency.

lines.s: Good afternoon. I'm going to talk about urban foxes, which have become a familiar sight in many British cities. Foxes first moved into towns in large numbers in the nineteen-thirties, when new suburbs with big gardens offered plenty of food and shelter. Today, researchers estimate that there are around one hundred and fifty thousand urban foxes in Britain. Contrary to popular belief, most of their diet isn't rubbish from bins — it's mainly worms, insects and small animals. Urban foxes are also surprisingly short-lived: the average fox survives only about eighteen months, and the biggest single cause of death is traffic. One question I'm often asked is whether foxes are dangerous to pets. In fact, conflicts with cats are rare, and the two animals usually ignore each other. Our current research uses tiny GPS collars to track foxes at night, and we've discovered that a single fox may cross more than twenty gardens in one evening. If you'd like to help, you can report sightings through our website.
lines.zh: 午安。我要談談城市狐狸，牠們在英國很多城市已經很常見。狐狸大量搬進城鎮是在 1930 年代，當時有大花園的新郊區提供了充足的食物和藏身處。現在研究人員估計英國約有十五萬隻城市狐狸。和一般人的想法相反，牠們的食物大多不是垃圾桶裡的垃圾，主要是蚯蚓、昆蟲和小動物。城市狐狸的壽命也短得出人意料：平均只活十八個月左右，最主要的死因是車禍。常有人問我狐狸會不會傷害寵物。事實上，牠們和貓起衝突很少見，兩者通常互不理睬。我們目前的研究用小型 GPS 項圈在夜間追蹤狐狸，發現一隻狐狸一個晚上可能穿過二十多個花園。如果想幫忙，可以透過我們的網站回報目擊紀錄。
lines.en: Good afternoon. I'm going to talk about urban foxes, which have become a familiar sight in many British cities. Foxes first moved into towns in large numbers in the nineteen-thirties, when new suburbs with big gardens offered plenty of food and shelter. Today, researchers estimate that there are around one hundred and fifty thousand urban foxes in Britain. Contrary to popular belief, most of their diet isn't rubbish from bins — it's mainly worms, insects and small animals. Urban foxes are also surprisingly short-lived: the average fox survives only about eighteen months, and the biggest single cause of death is traffic. One question I'm often asked is whether foxes are dangerous to pets. In fact, conflicts with cats are rare, and the two animals usually ignore each other. Our current research uses tiny GPS collars to track foxes at night, and we've discovered that a single fox may cross more than twenty gardens in one evening. If you'd like to help, you can report sightings through our website.

lines.s: Joining me today is the novelist Helen Price, whose new book has just won a major prize. Helen, you were a lawyer for fifteen years before you published anything. What made you change?
lines.zh: 今天的來賓是小說家海倫·普萊斯，她的新書剛得了一個大獎。海倫，你出版作品前當了十五年律師，是什麼讓你轉換跑道？
lines.en: Joining me today is the novelist Helen Price, whose new book has just won a major prize. Helen, you were a lawyer for fifteen years before you published anything. What made you change?

lines.s: I'd always written in secret, but I never thought of it as a career. Then I was on a long case that collapsed after two years, and I remember thinking: I've spent two years of my life on something that came to nothing. I didn't want to feel that way about my writing, so I took it seriously for the first time.
lines.zh: 我一直偷偷在寫，但從沒想過當成職業。後來我接了一個拖了兩年的案子，結果不了了之，我記得當時想：我花了兩年生命在一件毫無結果的事上。我不想對寫作也有這種感覺，所以第一次認真看待它。
lines.en: I'd always written in secret, but I never thought of it as a career. Then I was on a long case that collapsed after two years, and I remember thinking: I've spent two years of my life on something that came to nothing. I didn't want to feel that way about my writing, so I took it seriously for the first time.

lines.s: Did your legal background help?
lines.zh: 你的法律背景有幫助嗎？
lines.en: Did your legal background help?

lines.s: Enormously, though not in the way people assume. It's not about knowing the law. It's that I spent years listening to people tell their stories, and noticing what they left out. That's what fiction is really about — the gaps.
lines.zh: 幫助非常大，但不是大家以為的那樣。不是因為懂法律，而是我多年來聽人講述他們的故事，並注意他們略過了什麼。小說真正在寫的就是這些——空白之處。
lines.en: Enormously, though not in the way people assume. It's not about knowing the law. It's that I spent years listening to people tell their stories, and noticing what they left out. That's what fiction is really about — the gaps.

lines.s: The book is set in a small fishing town. Why there?
lines.zh: 這本書以一個小漁港為背景，為什麼選那裡？
lines.en: The book is set in a small fishing town. Why there?

lines.s: I grew up somewhere very similar, but I deliberately avoided my own town. I wanted the freedom to invent. Real places come with real neighbours, and I didn't want anyone recognising themselves.
lines.zh: 我在很類似的地方長大，但刻意避開了自己的家鄉。我想要自由虛構的空間。真實的地方就有真實的鄰居，我不希望有人認出自己。
lines.en: I grew up somewhere very similar, but I deliberately avoided my own town. I wanted the freedom to invent. Real places come with real neighbours, and I didn't want anyone recognising themselves.

lines.s: And what's next?
lines.zh: 接下來呢？
lines.en: And what's next?

lines.s: I'm superstitious about discussing work in progress. All I'll say is that it's shorter, and that I'm enjoying it more than I should be.
lines.zh: 我對談正在寫的作品有點迷信。只能說它比較短，而且我寫得比應該的還要開心。
lines.en: I'm superstitious about discussing work in progress. All I'll say is that it's shorter, and that I'm enjoying it more than I should be.

ask.en: Why did Helen start to take her writing seriously?

explain.zh: 兩年的案子不了了之，她不想對寫作也有同樣的感覺：重新看待時間。

ask.en: What does she say fiction is really about?

ask.en: Why did she not set the book in her own town?

lines.s: Speaker 1
lines.zh: 說話者 1
lines.en: Speaker 1

lines.s: I took up long-distance swimming after my doctor said my back problems would improve with exercise. I was hopeless at first, and I failed to finish my first open-water race. Oddly, that was the best thing that could have happened — it showed me exactly what I needed to work on.
lines.zh: 醫生說運動能改善我的背痛，我才開始長泳。一開始我很差，第一次公開水域比賽沒游完。奇怪的是，那是最好的事——它讓我清楚知道該加強什麼。
lines.en: I took up long-distance swimming after my doctor said my back problems would improve with exercise. I was hopeless at first, and I failed to finish my first open-water race. Oddly, that was the best thing that could have happened — it showed me exactly what I needed to work on.

lines.s: Speaker 2
lines.zh: 說話者 2
lines.en: Speaker 2

lines.s: My brother bet me I couldn't cycle from London to Paris, so of course I had to do it. The training took over my life for months. What I learnt, more than anything, was that I couldn't do it alone — the moment I joined a club and let others help me, everything got easier.
lines.zh: 我哥打賭我騎不完倫敦到巴黎，我當然非騎不可。訓練佔據了我好幾個月的生活。我學到最多的是，我沒辦法一個人做到——一加入車隊、讓別人幫我，一切就變簡單了。
lines.en: My brother bet me I couldn't cycle from London to Paris, so of course I had to do it. The training took over my life for months. What I learnt, more than anything, was that I couldn't do it alone — the moment I joined a club and let others help me, everything got easier.

lines.s: Speaker 3
lines.zh: 說話者 3
lines.en: Speaker 3

lines.s: I started gardening because my job in finance was so intense — I needed something slow. What it's taught me is that you can't hurry anything. Plants grow at their own pace, and I've become much calmer with my team at work as a result.
lines.zh: 我開始種花是因為金融工作太緊繃，我需要慢一點的東西。它教會我任何事都急不得。植物照自己的速度長，結果我對工作上的團隊也變得有耐心多了。
lines.en: I started gardening because my job in finance was so intense — I needed something slow. What it's taught me is that you can't hurry anything. Plants grow at their own pace, and I've become much calmer with my team at work as a result.

lines.s: Speaker 4
lines.zh: 說話者 4
lines.en: Speaker 4

lines.s: A friend dragged me along to a chess club, and I only went to keep him company. I assumed I'd hate it. But I've learnt to rely on my own instincts — there's no one to ask in the middle of a game, and that's been useful in every part of my life.
lines.zh: 一個朋友硬拉我去西洋棋社，我只是去陪他。我以為會討厭它。但我學會了相信自己的直覺——下棋到一半沒人可以問，這在我生活的每個方面都很有用。
lines.en: A friend dragged me along to a chess club, and I only went to keep him company. I assumed I'd hate it. But I've learnt to rely on my own instincts — there's no one to ask in the middle of a game, and that's been useful in every part of my life.

lines.s: Speaker 5
lines.zh: 說話者 5
lines.en: Speaker 5

lines.s: I read an article about people who walk the whole coastline of Wales, and decided on the spot to try. I'd always been someone who planned everything in detail, but you can't plan for the weather or for blisters. I learnt that a few small adjustments each day matter far more than a perfect plan.
lines.zh: 我讀到一篇文章，寫有人走完整條威爾斯海岸線，當場就決定也要試試。我一直是凡事詳細計畫的人，可是天氣和腳起水泡是沒辦法計畫的。我學到，每天做一點小調整，比完美的計畫重要得多。
lines.en: I read an article about people who walk the whole coastline of Wales, and decided on the spot to try. I'd always been someone who planned everything in detail, but you can't plan for the weather or for blisters. I learnt that a few small adjustments each day matter far more than a perfect plan.

lines.s: The trainer clearly knew her stuff, I'll give her that. But so much of it was common sense dressed up in jargon.

lines.s: You hear a writer talking about researching a biography.

lines.s: When I began researching the composer's life, I assumed his letters would be the most revealing source. In fact they were rather guarded — he knew they might be published one day. It was his household accounts that told me the most: what a person spends money on, and when, says a great deal about their priorities. I've since become slightly obsessed with receipts.
lines.zh: 我開始研究這位作曲家的生平時，以為他的信會是最能透露真相的資料。事實上那些信寫得很保留，他知道有一天可能會出版。告訴我最多的反而是他的家用帳本：一個人把錢花在什麼上、什麼時候花，很能說明他重視什麼。從那之後我就有點迷上收據了。
lines.en: When I began researching the composer's life, I assumed his letters would be the most revealing source. In fact they were rather guarded — he knew they might be published one day. lines.s: Hello. I'm going to talk about the Northern Star, a merchant ship that sank off the coast of Cornwall in 1762. It was discovered in 2014 by two amateur divers who were actually looking for a different wreck. The ship lies at a depth of about thirty metres, which means divers can only work for around twenty minutes at a time. Visibility is often poor, so much of the work is done by touch. The most surprising discovery so far has been a box of oranges, still recognisable after more than two hundred and fifty years, thanks to the cold, airless mud. We've also recovered over four hundred pieces of china, which tell us the ship was returning from Portugal. One of the biggest challenges is protecting the site from treasure hunters, so its exact location is kept secret. Next summer we plan to use underwater cameras to create a three-dimensional model, so that the public can explore the wreck online.
lines.zh: 大家好。我要談談「北極星號」，一艘 1762 年在康瓦耳外海沉沒的商船。它在 2014 年被兩位業餘潛水員發現，他們其實是在找另一艘沉船。船沉在大約三十公尺深的地方，所以潛水員一次只能工作二十分鐘左右。能見度常常很差，所以很多工作是靠觸摸完成的。目前最令人意外的發現是一箱柳橙，在冰冷缺氧的泥巴保護下，兩百五十多年後仍然認得出來。我們也找回了四百多件瓷器，顯示這艘船是從葡萄牙返航的。最大的挑戰之一是保護遺址不被尋寶者破壞，所以確切位置是保密的。明年夏天我們打算用水下攝影機建立一個立體模型，讓大眾可以在網路上探索這艘沉船。
lines.en: Hello. I'm going to talk about the Northern Star, a merchant ship that sank off the coast of Cornwall in 1762. It was discovered in 2014 by two amateur divers who were actually looking for a different wreck. The ship lies at a depth of about thirty metres, which means divers can only work for around twenty minutes at a time. Visibility is often poor, so much of the work is done by touch. The most surprising discovery so far has been a box of oranges, still recognisable after more than two hundred and fifty years, thanks to the cold, airless mud. We've also recovered over four hundred pieces of china, which tell us the ship was returning from Portugal. One of the biggest challenges is protecting the site from treasure hunters, so its exact location is kept secret. Next summer we plan to use underwater cameras to create a three-dimensional model, so that the public can explore the wreck online.

lines.s: My guest is Rosa Lind, an architect known for her school buildings. Rosa, what first drew you to designing schools?
lines.zh: 今天的來賓是以設計校舍聞名的建築師羅莎·林德。羅莎，最初是什麼吸引你設計學校？
lines.en: My guest is Rosa Lind, an architect known for her school buildings. Rosa, what first drew you to designing schools?

lines.s: Honestly, a bad experience. My own secondary school was a grim concrete block with tiny windows, and I was miserable there. Years later, as a young architect, I visited a school in Denmark full of light and wood, and the children seemed completely different. I thought: buildings can't be irrelevant to how people feel.
lines.zh: 老實說是一段不好的經驗。我念的中學是一棟陰沉的水泥建築，窗戶很小，我在那裡過得很痛苦。多年後我還是年輕建築師時，去參觀丹麥一所充滿光線和木頭的學校，那裡的孩子完全不一樣。我心想：建築不可能和人的感受無關。
lines.en: Honestly, a bad experience. My own secondary school was a grim concrete block with tiny windows, and I was miserable there. Years later, as a young architect, I visited a school in Denmark full of light and wood, and the children seemed completely different. I thought: buildings can't be irrelevant to how people feel.

lines.s: What do you do first on a new project?
lines.zh: 接到新案子時你先做什麼？
lines.en: What do you do first on a new project?

lines.s: I spend at least a week in the existing school, just watching. Where do children gather at break? Which corridors get blocked? Teachers often tell me one thing, but the way people actually move tells me another.
lines.zh: 我至少花一週待在原本的學校裡，就只是觀察。下課時孩子聚在哪裡？哪些走廊會塞住？老師常告訴我一件事，但人們實際的動線告訴我的是另一件事。
lines.en: I spend at least a week in the existing school, just watching. Where do children gather at break? Which corridors get blocked? Teachers often tell me one thing, but the way people actually move tells me another.

lines.s: Is there a feature you always include?
lines.zh: 有沒有什麼設計你一定會放？
lines.en: Is there a feature you always include?

lines.s: Places to be alone. We design schools as if every child wants to be in a crowd, but many of them don't. A small window seat or a quiet corner can make a huge difference to a shy child.
lines.zh: 可以獨處的地方。我們設計學校時好像每個孩子都想待在人群裡，但很多孩子並不想。一個窗邊的小座位或一個安靜的角落，對害羞的孩子影響很大。
lines.en: Places to be alone. We design schools as if every child wants to be in a crowd, but many of them don't. A small window seat or a quiet corner can make a huge difference to a shy child.

lines.s: Some critics say your buildings are too expensive.
lines.zh: 有些批評者說你的建築太貴了。
lines.en: Some critics say your buildings are too expensive.

lines.s: They can cost more at the start, I admit. But they use far less energy, and the materials last longer, so over thirty years they usually work out cheaper. The problem is that budgets are set for a single year.
lines.zh: 我承認一開始可能比較貴。但它們耗能少得多，材料也更耐用，所以三十年下來通常反而比較便宜。問題在於預算是一年一年編的。
lines.en: They can cost more at the start, I admit. But they use far less energy, and the materials last longer, so over thirty years they usually work out cheaper. The problem is that budgets are set for a single year.

lines.s: What's been your biggest mistake?
lines.zh: 你最大的失誤是什麼？
lines.en: What's been your biggest mistake?

lines.s: An open-plan library I was very proud of. It looked wonderful in photographs, but it was so noisy that nobody could read in it. We had to add glass walls a year later. I learnt to trust photographs less and teachers more.
lines.zh: 一間我很得意的開放式圖書館。照片上看起來很棒，可是吵到沒人能在裡面看書。一年後我們只好加裝玻璃牆。我學到要少相信照片，多相信老師。
lines.en: An open-plan library I was very proud of. It looked wonderful in photographs, but it was so noisy that nobody could read in it. We had to add glass walls a year later. I learnt to trust photographs less and teachers more.

ask.s: Why did Rosa become interested in designing schools?
ask.zh: 羅莎為什麼對設計學校有興趣？
ask.en: Why did Rosa become interested in designing schools?

options.t: She had always wanted to be a teacher.
A visit made her see how buildings affect people.
She was asked to redesign her old school.

explain.zh: 參觀丹麥的學校，讓她覺得「建築不可能和人的感受無關」。
explain.en: A Danish school showed her buildings affect feelings.

ask.s: What does she do at the start of each project?
ask.zh: 每個案子開始時她做什麼？
ask.en: What does she do at the start of each project?

options.t: She studies plans of other schools.
She observes how the school is used.
She asks children to draw their ideal school.

explain.zh: 「至少花一週待在原本的學校裡，就只是觀察」。

ask.s: What does she say about teachers' descriptions of their school?
ask.zh: 她怎麼說老師對學校的描述？
ask.en: What does she say about teachers' descriptions of their school?

options.t: They do not always match how space is really used.
They are usually ignored by architects.
They matter more than children's views.
They tend to ask for more classrooms.

explain.zh: 老師說一件事，「人們實際的動線告訴我的是另一件事」。
explain.en: What teachers say and how people move can differ.

ask.s: What feature does she always include?
ask.zh: 她一定會放什麼設計？
ask.en: What feature does she always include?

explain.zh: 「可以獨處的地方」，例如窗邊小座位、安靜角落。

ask.s: How does she respond to criticism about cost?
ask.zh: 她怎麼回應成本的批評？
ask.en: How does she respond to criticism about cost?

options.t: She accepts her buildings are too expensive.
She says the materials are cheap.
She says long-term savings make up for it.

explain.zh: 一開始較貴，但「三十年下來通常反而比較便宜」。

ask.s: What did she learn from the library?
ask.zh: 她從圖書館學到什麼？
ask.en: What did she learn from the library?

options.t: How a space works matters more than how it looks.
Libraries should be separate from the main building.

explain.zh: 照片上很棒卻吵到沒人能讀書：「少相信照片，多相信老師」。

lines.s: Speaker 1
lines.zh: 說話者 1
lines.en: Speaker 1

lines.s: I'd always been rather dismissive of people who couldn't manage their money. Then my business failed, and I lost almost everything. It's humbling to realise how quickly it can happen. These days I volunteer at a debt advice centre two evenings a week — I want to make sure nobody feels as alone as I did.
lines.zh: 我以前一直很看不起不會理財的人。後來我的生意失敗，幾乎失去了一切。發現事情可以來得這麼快，讓人很謙卑。現在我每週兩個晚上在債務諮詢中心當志工，我想確保沒有人像我當時那麼孤單。
lines.en: I'd always been rather dismissive of people who couldn't manage their money. Then my business failed, and I lost almost everything. It's humbling to realise how quickly it can happen. These days I volunteer at a debt advice centre two evenings a week — I want to make sure nobody feels as alone as I did.

lines.s: Speaker 2
lines.zh: 說話者 2
lines.en: Speaker 2

lines.s: I used to think travel was a waste of money — why go abroad when you can watch documentaries? Then my company sent me to Vietnam for a month, and I came back a different person. When I remember the lectures I used to give my friends about it, I can only laugh at myself.
lines.zh: 我以前覺得旅行是浪費錢，看紀錄片就好，何必出國？後來公司派我去越南一個月，回來後我像變了一個人。想起以前對朋友說的那些大道理，我只能笑自己。
lines.en: I used to think travel was a waste of money — why go abroad when you can watch documentaries? Then my company sent me to Vietnam for a month, and I came back a different person. When I remember the lectures I used to give my friends about it, I can only laugh at myself.

lines.s: Speaker 3
lines.zh: 說話者 3
lines.en: Speaker 3

lines.s: I was firmly against having children; I thought it would end my career. Then, at thirty-eight, I found myself pregnant. I won't pretend the first year was easy, and I still don't know whether I've made the right choices about work. Ask me again in ten years.
lines.zh: 我以前堅決不要孩子，覺得那會終結我的事業。後來三十八歲時我懷孕了。我不會假裝第一年很輕鬆，而且到現在我還不知道自己在工作上的選擇對不對。十年後再問我吧。
lines.en: I was firmly against having children; I thought it would end my career. Then, at thirty-eight, I found myself pregnant. I won't pretend the first year was easy, and I still don't know whether I've made the right choices about work. Ask me again in ten years.

lines.s: Speaker 4
lines.zh: 說話者 4
lines.en: Speaker 4

lines.s: My father had told me for years to retrain, and I'd ignored him. It took a stranger on a long train journey — a nurse who'd changed career at fifty — to make me actually listen. I'm thankful every day that I sat in that seat.
lines.zh: 我爸多年來一直叫我去學新技能轉行，我都不理他。結果是長途火車上的一個陌生人——一位五十歲才轉行的護理師——讓我真的聽進去。我每天都很感謝自己坐了那個位子。
lines.en: My father had told me for years to retrain, and I'd ignored him. It took a stranger on a long train journey — a nurse who'd changed career at fifty — to make me actually listen. I'm thankful every day that I sat in that seat.

lines.s: Speaker 5
lines.zh: 說話者 5
lines.en: Speaker 5

lines.s: I'd always laughed at people who worried about diets and wellness. Then I was diagnosed with diabetes, and suddenly what I ate really mattered. I was rude to a lot of people who tried to help me early on, and I still cringe when I think about it.
lines.zh: 我以前總是嘲笑那些在意飲食和養生的人。後來我被診斷出糖尿病，突然間吃什麼變得很重要。一開始很多人想幫我，我卻對他們很沒禮貌，現在想起來還是很尷尬。
lines.en: I'd always laughed at people who worried about diets and wellness. Then I was diagnosed with diabetes, and suddenly what I ate really mattered. I was rude to a lot of people who tried to help me early on, and I still cringe when I think about it.

lines.s: People assume the satisfaction comes when a piece is finished and gleaming. For me, it's the stage before that — taking it apart and discovering how it was made. You find pencil marks the original carpenter left, sometimes a date. You feel a connection to someone who's been dead for two hundred years. The finished chair almost feels like an anticlimax.
lines.zh: 大家以為成就感來自家具修好、閃閃發亮的時候。對我來說是在那之前的階段：把它拆開，發現它是怎麼做的。你會找到原本的木匠留下的鉛筆記號，有時還有日期。你會覺得和一個死了兩百年的人有了連結。完成的椅子反而有點讓人失落。

lines.s: Today I'm going to talk about the Fleetwater, a river that once ran through the middle of our city but has been hidden underground for more than a century. In the Middle Ages, the river was used by tanners, whose work made the water so polluted that people called it the Black Brook. By the eighteen-sixties it was little more than an open sewer, and after an outbreak of cholera the city council decided to cover it over. Today it flows through a brick tunnel about two metres wide. You can still hear it in a few places: there's a metal grate outside the central library where, on a quiet day, the sound of water is surprisingly loud. Several groups are now campaigning to bring the river back to the surface. They point to cities like Seoul, where uncovering a river created a popular park and actually lowered summer temperatures nearby. The main obstacle, of course, is cost — the latest estimate is around forty million pounds. A public consultation will begin in March.
lines.zh: 今天我要談談弗利特河，一條曾經流經市中心、但已經藏在地底一百多年的河。中世紀時，這條河被製革工人使用，他們的工作把河水汙染得很嚴重，大家都叫它「黑溪」。到了 1860 年代，它幾乎只是一條露天下水道，霍亂爆發後，市議會決定把它加蓋。現在它流經一條大約兩公尺寬的磚砌隧道。有幾個地方還聽得到它：中央圖書館外有一個金屬格柵，安靜的日子裡，水聲大得令人驚訝。現在有好幾個團體在推動讓這條河重見天日。他們舉首爾等城市為例，在那裡揭開河道後不但成了熱門的公園，還降低了附近的夏季氣溫。當然最大的障礙是成本，最新估計大約四千萬英鎊。公眾諮詢將在三月開始。
lines.en: Today I'm going to talk about the Fleetwater, a river that once ran through the middle of our city but has been hidden underground for more than a century. In the Middle Ages, the river was used by tanners, whose work made the water so polluted that people called it the Black Brook. By the eighteen-sixties it was little more than an open sewer, and after an outbreak of cholera the city council decided to cover it over. Today it flows through a brick tunnel about two metres wide. You can still hear it in a few places: there's a metal grate outside the central library where, on a quiet day, the sound of water is surprisingly loud. Several groups are now campaigning to bring the river back to the surface. They point to cities like Seoul, where uncovering a river created a popular park and actually lowered summer temperatures nearby. The main obstacle, of course, is cost — the latest estimate is around forty million pounds. A public consultation will begin in March.

lines.s: With me is Ines Ferreira, who has translated more than forty novels from Portuguese into English. Ines, how did you start?
lines.zh: 今天的來賓是伊內絲·費雷拉，她把四十多本小說從葡萄牙文翻成英文。伊內絲，你是怎麼開始的？
lines.en: With me is Ines Ferreira, who has translated more than forty novels from Portuguese into English. Ines, how did you start?

lines.s: By accident. I was teaching English in Lisbon, and a friend asked me to translate a short story she'd written, just for fun. A publisher happened to read it in a magazine and contacted me. I had no training at all — I learnt on the job, mostly by making mistakes.
lines.zh: 純屬意外。我當時在里斯本教英文，一個朋友請我翻譯她寫的一篇短篇小說，只是好玩。一位出版商剛好在雜誌上讀到，就聯絡了我。我完全沒受過訓練，都是邊做邊學，大多是靠犯錯學的。
lines.en: By accident. I was teaching English in Lisbon, and a friend asked me to translate a short story she'd written, just for fun. A publisher happened to read it in a magazine and contacted me. I had no training at all — I learnt on the job, mostly by making mistakes.

lines.s: What's the hardest thing to translate?
lines.zh: 最難翻的是什麼？
lines.en: What's the hardest thing to translate?

lines.s: People expect me to say jokes or wordplay, and those are hard. But the real difficulty is rhythm. Every writer has a particular music in their sentences, and if you lose that, you lose the book, even if every word is technically correct.
lines.zh: 大家以為我會說笑話或文字遊戲，那些確實難。但真正的難處是節奏。每個作家的句子都有獨特的音樂性，失去了它，就失去了整本書，即使每個字在技術上都是對的。
lines.en: People expect me to say jokes or wordplay, and those are hard. But the real difficulty is rhythm. Every writer has a particular music in their sentences, and if you lose that, you lose the book, even if every word is technically correct.

lines.s: Do you work closely with authors?
lines.zh: 你會和作者密切合作嗎？
lines.en: Do you work closely with authors?

lines.s: When they're alive and willing! Some love being involved and answer dozens of emails. Others say, 'It's your book now,' and leave me alone. Oddly, I find the second kind more frightening.
lines.zh: 如果他們還在世又願意的話！有些作者很喜歡參與，會回覆幾十封信。也有人說「現在這是你的書了」，就放手不管。奇怪的是，我覺得第二種更可怕。
lines.en: When they're alive and willing! Some love being involved and answer dozens of emails. Others say, 'It's your book now,' and leave me alone. Oddly, I find the second kind more frightening.

lines.s: Translators' names rarely appear on covers. Does that bother you?
lines.zh: 譯者的名字很少出現在封面上，這會困擾你嗎？
lines.en: Translators' names rarely appear on covers. Does that bother you?

lines.s: It used to. But things are changing — more publishers now put our names on the front, and readers are more aware that they're reading a translation. I'd rather campaign for fair pay, though; that matters more than fame.
lines.zh: 以前會。但情況在改變，越來越多出版商把我們的名字放在封面上，讀者也更清楚自己讀的是譯本。不過我更想爭取合理的報酬，那比名氣重要。
lines.en: It used to. But things are changing — more publishers now put our names on the front, and readers are more aware that they're reading a translation. I'd rather campaign for fair pay, though; that matters more than fame.

lines.s: What advice would you give a new translator?
lines.zh: 你會給新譯者什麼建議？
lines.en: What advice would you give a new translator?

lines.s: Read widely in your own language, not just the one you translate from. Your English is your instrument; it has to be perfectly in tune.
lines.zh: 多讀自己母語的書，不只是你翻譯的那種語言。你的英文就是你的樂器，它必須完全調準音。
lines.en: Read widely in your own language, not just the one you translate from. Your English is your instrument; it has to be perfectly in tune.

lines.s: Speaker 1
lines.zh: 說話者 1
lines.en: Speaker 1

lines.s: When the factory closed, I had a redundancy payment and no idea what to do. I'd done a bit of mechanics in the army, so I rented a garage and started repairing bikes. The hardest part wasn't the work — it was the paperwork. Licences, insurance, safety inspections... I spent more time on forms than on bikes in the first year.
lines.zh: 工廠關門時，我拿到一筆資遣費，完全不知道該做什麼。我在軍中做過一點機械，所以租了一間車庫開始修腳踏車。最難的不是工作本身，而是文書作業。執照、保險、安全檢查……第一年我花在表格上的時間比花在腳踏車上還多。
lines.en: When the factory closed, I had a redundancy payment and no idea what to do. I'd done a bit of mechanics in the army, so I rented a garage and started repairing bikes. The hardest part wasn't the work — it was the paperwork. Licences, insurance, safety inspections... I spent more time on forms than on bikes in the first year.

lines.s: Speaker 2
lines.zh: 說話者 2
lines.en: Speaker 2

lines.s: I noticed there wasn't a single shop in town selling clothes for tall women — and I'm six foot one. So I opened one. People said I was mad, but it was obvious there was demand. My problem has been letting people know we exist; most of my customers still find us by chance.
lines.zh: 我發現鎮上沒有一家店賣高個子女生的衣服，而我有一百八十五公分。所以我就開了一家。大家說我瘋了，但需求明明就在那裡。我的問題是讓大家知道我們的存在，大部分客人到現在還是偶然發現我們的。
lines.en: I noticed there wasn't a single shop in town selling clothes for tall women — and I'm six foot one. So I opened one. People said I was mad, but it was obvious there was demand. My problem has been letting people know we exist; most of my customers still find us by chance.

lines.s: Speaker 3
lines.zh: 說話者 3
lines.en: Speaker 3

lines.s: I was a lawyer for twelve years, and I was bored out of my mind. I opened the bakery mainly because I needed a change of direction. The hardest thing is the hours — I start at four, and I barely see my kids before bedtime.
lines.zh: 我當了十二年律師，無聊得要命。我開麵包店主要是因為需要轉換方向。最難的是工時，我四點開工，孩子睡前幾乎見不到他們。
lines.en: I was a lawyer for twelve years, and I was bored out of my mind. I opened the bakery mainly because I needed a change of direction. The hardest thing is the hours — I start at four, and I barely see my kids before bedtime.

lines.s: Speaker 4
lines.zh: 說話者 4
lines.en: Speaker 4

lines.s: My mother ran a small café for thirty years, and when she got ill, someone had to keep it going. I never planned to run a business. The most difficult thing has been money — there are weeks when the bills arrive before the customers do.
lines.zh: 我媽媽經營一家小咖啡館三十年，她生病時總得有人撐下去。我從沒打算做生意。最難的是錢，有些星期帳單比客人先到。
lines.en: My mother ran a small café for thirty years, and when she got ill, someone had to keep it going. I never planned to run a business. The most difficult thing has been money — there are weeks when the bills arrive before the customers do.

lines.s: Speaker 5
lines.zh: 說話者 5
lines.en: Speaker 5

lines.s: I'd been selling my photographs to friends for years, and one of my regular buyers, who owns a gallery, suggested I sell prints online. Now it's my full-time job. What I miss is having colleagues — some days the only person I speak to is the postman.
lines.zh: 我多年來一直把照片賣給朋友，有一位常客開藝廊，他建議我在網路上賣版畫。現在這成了我的全職工作。我想念的是有同事，有些日子我唯一說話的對象是郵差。
lines.en: I'd been selling my photographs to friends for years, and one of my regular buyers, who owns a gallery, suggested I sell prints online. Now it's my full-time job. What I miss is having colleagues — some days the only person I speak to is the postman.

lines.s: I know what you mean. Though I'd say the facts needed saying — most people have no idea how bad things are.

lines.en: I know what you mean. Though I'd say the facts needed saying — most people have no idea how bad things are.

lines.s: Maybe. I just think showing is more powerful than telling. The scene with the turtles said more than any narration.
lines.zh: 也許吧。我只是覺得呈現比說教更有力，海龜那一幕勝過任何旁白。
lines.en: Maybe. I just think showing is more powerful than telling. The scene with the turtles said more than any narration.

lines.s: You hear a woman talking about her experience of a writing course.
lines.zh: 你聽到一位女士談她上寫作課的經驗。
lines.en: You hear a woman talking about her experience of a writing course.

lines.s: I'd assumed the tutor would focus on grammar and style, which frankly I didn't need. Instead she made us write every day for twenty minutes without stopping, and without reading it back. It felt pointless at first. By the third week I realised I'd stopped censoring myself, and some of what I wrote was genuinely surprising. I can't say my sentences improved much, but I'm far less afraid of the blank page.
lines.zh: 我以為講師會著重文法和風格，老實說那我不需要。結果她要我們每天寫二十分鐘，不停筆，也不回頭讀。一開始覺得沒意義。到第三週我發現自己不再自我審查，寫出的東西有些真的令人驚喜。我不能說句子進步多少，但我不再那麼害怕空白頁了。

It felt pointless at first. By the third week I realised I'd stopped censoring myself, and some of what I wrote was genuinely surprising. lines.s: You will hear a marine biologist called Dr Helen Ross talking about her research on seagrass.
lines.zh: 你會聽到海洋生物學家海倫·羅斯博士談她對海草的研究。
lines.en: You will hear a marine biologist called Dr Helen Ross talking about her research on seagrass.

lines.s: Most people have never heard of seagrass, yet these underwater meadows are among the most valuable habitats on the planet. I first became interested as a student, when I joined a project counting seahorses, which live among the grass. What surprised me most was learning that seagrass absorbs carbon around thirty-five times faster than tropical rainforest. Unfortunately, we've lost about a third of the world's seagrass in the last century, mainly because of pollution from farming, which makes the water cloudy and blocks sunlight. Boats are another problem: anchors tear up the plants, so we've introduced special moorings in several bays. Our restoration work involves collecting seeds by hand — volunteers dive in late summer, when the seeds are ripe — and planting them in hessian bags, which break down naturally. In our first trial, only ten per cent of the seeds grew, but last year the figure reached sixty per cent. The project depends on local fishermen, who were suspicious at first but now help us monitor the sites, because healthy seagrass means more fish. My next goal is to map every meadow along the south coast within five years.
lines.zh: 大多數人沒聽過海草，但這些水下草原是地球上最有價值的棲地之一。我學生時代參加一個計算海馬的計畫，海馬就住在草間，從此開始感興趣。最讓我驚訝的是海草吸收碳的速度約是熱帶雨林的三十五倍。可惜上個世紀全球失去了約三分之一的海草，主要是農業汙染讓海水混濁、擋住陽光。船也是問題：錨會扯壞植物，所以我們在幾個海灣設置了特殊繫泊設施。我們的復育工作是手工採集種子——志工在夏末種子成熟時潛水採集——再種在會自然分解的麻布袋裡。第一次試驗只有百分之十的種子長出來，但去年達到百分之六十。計畫仰賴當地漁民，他們起初很懷疑，現在幫我們監測地點，因為健康的海草代表更多魚。我的下一個目標是五年內繪製南部海岸每一片海草床的地圖。
lines.en: Most people have never heard of seagrass, yet these underwater meadows are among the most valuable habitats on the planet. I first became interested as a student, when I joined a project counting seahorses, which live among the grass. What surprised me most was learning that seagrass absorbs carbon around thirty-five times faster than tropical rainforest. Unfortunately, we've lost about a third of the world's seagrass in the last century, mainly because of pollution from farming, which makes the water cloudy and blocks sunlight. Boats are another problem: anchors tear up the plants, so we've introduced special moorings in several bays. Our restoration work involves collecting seeds by hand — volunteers dive in late summer, when the seeds are ripe — and planting them in hessian bags, which break down naturally. In our first trial, only ten per cent of the seeds grew, but last year the figure reached sixty per cent. The project depends on local fishermen, who were suspicious at first but now help us monitor the sites, because healthy seagrass means more fish. My next goal is to map every meadow along the south coast within five years.

lines.s: You will hear an interview with an architect called David Lee about designing homes for older people.
lines.zh: 你會聽到建築師李大衛談為長者設計住宅的訪問。
lines.en: You will hear an interview with an architect called David Lee about designing homes for older people.

lines.s: David, why did you start specialising in homes for older people?
lines.zh: 大衛，你為什麼開始專門設計長者住宅？
lines.en: David, why did you start specialising in homes for older people?

lines.s: Honestly, it was my mother. When she struggled with the stairs in her house, I realised how little the buildings I'd designed considered people like her. It was quite a humbling moment.
lines.zh: 老實說是因為我母親。她在家爬樓梯很吃力時，我才發現我設計的建築多麼少考慮到她這樣的人。那一刻讓我很慚愧。
lines.en: Honestly, it was my mother. When she struggled with the stairs in her house, I realised how little the buildings I'd designed considered people like her. It was quite a humbling moment.

lines.s: What's the most common mistake in housing for older people?
lines.zh: 長者住宅最常見的錯誤是什麼？
lines.en: What's the most common mistake in housing for older people?

lines.s: Making it look like a hospital. Grab rails and ramps are important, but if everything is grey and clinical, people feel they've stopped living and started waiting. Design should feel like home first.
lines.zh: 弄得像醫院。扶手和坡道很重要，但如果什麼都是灰色、冷冰冰的，人會覺得自己不再是在生活，而是在等待。設計首先要有家的感覺。
lines.en: Making it look like a hospital. Grab rails and ramps are important, but if everything is grey and clinical, people feel they've stopped living and started waiting. Design should feel like home first.

lines.s: You often talk about "shared spaces". Why are they important?
lines.zh: 你常談「共享空間」，為什麼重要？
lines.en: You often talk about "shared spaces". Why are they important?

lines.s: Loneliness is as damaging to health as smoking, according to some studies. A shared garden or kitchen gives people a reason to come out of their flats — but it must be optional. Nobody wants to be forced to socialise.
lines.zh: 有研究說孤獨對健康的傷害和吸菸一樣。共享花園或廚房讓人有理由走出公寓，但必須是自願的，沒人想被迫社交。
lines.en: Loneliness is as damaging to health as smoking, according to some studies. A shared garden or kitchen gives people a reason to come out of their flats — but it must be optional. Nobody wants to be forced to socialise.

lines.s: Are these homes more expensive to build?
lines.zh: 這種住宅蓋起來比較貴嗎？
lines.en: Are these homes more expensive to build?

lines.s: Slightly, at the start. But if people can stay independent for longer, the savings on care are enormous. The problem is that the people who pay for the building aren't the ones who save the money later.
lines.zh: 一開始稍微貴一點。但如果人們能更久地獨立生活，照護費省下的錢很可觀。問題是出錢蓋房子的人，不是日後省到錢的人。
lines.en: Slightly, at the start. But if people can stay independent for longer, the savings on care are enormous. The problem is that the people who pay for the building aren't the ones who save the money later.

lines.s: What are you working on now?
lines.zh: 你現在在做什麼？
lines.en: What are you working on now?

lines.s: A building where students and retired people live together. The students pay lower rent in return for a few hours a week helping their neighbours. We'll see whether it works — I'm hopeful, but it's an experiment.
lines.zh: 一棟學生和退休人士同住的建築。學生付較低的房租，換每週幾小時幫助鄰居。我們看看行不行得通，我抱持希望，但這是一個實驗。
lines.en: A building where students and retired people live together. The students pay lower rent in return for a few hours a week helping their neighbours. We'll see whether it works — I'm hopeful, but it's an experiment.

ask.s: What led David to specialise in housing for older people?
ask.zh: 是什麼讓大衛專攻長者住宅？
ask.en: What led David to specialise in housing for older people?

explain.zh: 「是因為我母親」爬樓梯吃力。

ask.zh: 大衛說最常見的錯誤是？
ask.en: What does David say is the most common mistake?

explain.zh: 「弄得像醫院」。

ask.s: What does David say about shared spaces?
ask.zh: 大衛對共享空間的看法？
ask.en: What does David say about shared spaces?

options.t: Residents should be free to choose whether to use them.
They should be used every day.
They are more important than private rooms.

explain.zh: 「必須是自願的」。

ask.zh: 大衛為什麼提到吸菸？
ask.en: Why does David mention smoking?

options.t: to show how harmful loneliness can be

explain.zh: 「孤獨對健康的傷害和吸菸一樣」。

ask.s: What problem does David identify with the cost of these homes?
ask.zh: 大衛指出成本上的什麼問題？
ask.en: What problem does David identify with the cost of these homes?

options.t: They are much too expensive to build.
The savings go to different people from those who pay.

explain.zh: 「出錢蓋房子的人，不是日後省到錢的人」。

ask.s: How does David feel about his current project?
ask.zh: 大衛對現在的計畫感覺如何？
ask.en: How does David feel about his current project?

explain.zh: 「我抱持希望，但這是一個實驗」。

lines.s: Speaker 1
lines.zh: 說話者 1
lines.en: Speaker 1

lines.s: When the factory closed, I was out of work for nearly a year. It was the worst time of my life, but it forced me to retrain, and I became a nurse. I'm much better at listening to people now — I know what it's like when nobody seems to care.
lines.zh: 工廠關門後，我失業將近一年，那是我人生最糟的時期，但它逼我轉職，我成了護理師。我現在更懂得傾聽別人——我知道沒人在乎是什麼感覺。
lines.en: When the factory closed, I was out of work for nearly a year. It was the worst time of my life, but it forced me to retrain, and I became a nurse. I'm much better at listening to people now — I know what it's like when nobody seems to care.

lines.s: Speaker 2
lines.zh: 說話者 2
lines.en: Speaker 2

lines.s: I met an old woman on a train who had travelled the world alone in her seventies. We only talked for an hour, but I booked my first solo trip the following week. I still write to her, and I always thank her — I wouldn't have dared without that conversation.
lines.zh: 我在火車上遇到一位七十多歲時獨自環遊世界的老太太。我們只聊了一小時，但我隔週就訂了第一次獨自旅行。我還在寫信給她，每次都謝謝她——沒有那次談話，我不敢踏出去。
lines.en: I met an old woman on a train who had travelled the world alone in her seventies. We only talked for an hour, but I booked my first solo trip the following week. I still write to her, and I always thank her — I wouldn't have dared without that conversation.

lines.s: Speaker 3
lines.zh: 說話者 3
lines.en: Speaker 3

lines.s: My teacher once wrote on my essay that I had a gift for explaining things. Nobody had ever said anything like that to me. I'm now a science journalist, and honestly I'm still amazed it worked out — I nearly failed school.
lines.zh: 老師曾在我的作文上寫，說我很有解釋事情的天分。從來沒人對我說過這種話。我現在是科學記者，老實說我還是很驚訝自己做到了——我差點就畢不了業。
lines.en: My teacher once wrote on my essay that I had a gift for explaining things. Nobody had ever said anything like that to me. I'm now a science journalist, and honestly I'm still amazed it worked out — I nearly failed school.

lines.s: Speaker 4
lines.zh: 說話者 4
lines.en: Speaker 4

lines.s: When my father became seriously ill, I moved back home to look after him. I gave up a job I loved. He recovered, and I've never gone back to my old career. To be honest, I'm glad — I was exhausted in that job and I'd never admitted it, even to myself.
lines.zh: 父親重病時，我搬回家照顧他，放棄了一份我很喜歡的工作。他康復了，我也沒再回到原本的職業。老實說我很慶幸——那份工作讓我精疲力盡，只是我從沒承認，連對自己也沒有。
lines.en: When my father became seriously ill, I moved back home to look after him. I gave up a job I loved. He recovered, and I've never gone back to my old career. To be honest, I'm glad — I was exhausted in that job and I'd never admitted it, even to myself.

lines.s: Speaker 5
lines.zh: 說話者 5
lines.en: Speaker 5

lines.s: I'd been worrying about money for years, and one night I read an article about a family who lived on almost nothing and seemed perfectly happy. We sold the house, moved somewhere smaller, and I've started giving talks about living simply. People need to hear that it's possible.
lines.zh: 我為錢煩惱了好多年，某天晚上讀到一篇文章，講一個幾乎沒什麼錢卻非常快樂的家庭。我們賣了房子搬到小一點的地方，我也開始演講談簡單生活。大家需要知道這是可能的。
lines.en: I'd been worrying about money for years, and one night I read an article about a family who lived on almost nothing and seemed perfectly happy. We sold the house, moved somewhere smaller, and I've started giving talks about living simply. People need to hear that it's possible.
